method: Verse-by-verse preliminary source-critical screening; original-language Hebrew and modern translations checked for two precise candidate passages; not a critical-edition or manuscript collation. No negative finding establishes absence across all traditions.

verses.finding: Israelites asked to consider clear signs given them; prior Exodus traditions broadly relevant, but no single passage verified as an exact counterpart.
Worldly life portrayed as attractive to disbelievers and believers mocked; broad moral motif; no source-specific parallel established.
Humanity once one community, then prophets and scripture sent amid disputes; comparative primeval and prophetic histories require deeper work.
Believers warned of hardship like those before them and ask when divine help will come; wilderness testing motif compared cautiously with Deuteronomy 8:2–3.
Question about charitable spending for parents, relatives, orphans, needy and travelers; ethical law, no specific verse-level predecessor assigned.
Fighting prescribed despite dislike; contested warfare law context, no precise earlier literary dependence asserted.
Questions about fighting in sacred month and expulsion from sanctuary; requires dated Arabian calendrical and sanctuary evidence.
Apostasy, death and punishment in afterlife; no verse-specific earlier primary passage established.
Questions concerning wine and gambling, acknowledging benefit but greater sin; Proverbs 23:29–35 warns of wine harms but does not address gambling or the same balancing formulation.
Questions concerning orphans and managing their welfare; Exodus 22:21–23 prohibits mistreating orphans, but does not regulate mixing their property with guardians.

candidates.reading: Sefaria Hebrew text and Revised JPS 2023 translation consulted; no critical manuscript collation
candidates.shared: Both treat consumption of wine as potentially harmful.
candidates.difference: Proverbs warns of drunkenness and its effects; Qur'an 2:219 weighs harm and benefit for wine and gambling together.
candidates.limits: No shared distinctive phrasing or borrowing established; modern translation not an ancient manuscript witness.

candidates.reading: Hebrew and English text cross-checked via Sefaria and Chabad; translation numbering differs by edition
candidates.shared: Both express responsibility toward vulnerable orphans.
candidates.difference: Exodus forbids oppression and threatens divine retribution; Qur'an 2:220 concerns their welfare and practical mixing of affairs with guardians.
candidates.limits: Do not equate ethical concern with identical guardianship law; textual witnesses and dating not collated.
